note: Paper 3: B=50 permutation null on Diabetes130US (was B=1).
predicted: Paper 3's central claim -- exploitable structure -0.0039 -- comes from oracle_ceiling.py, which draws ONE mask permutation per dataset and then Mann-Whitney tests its 15 fold-gains against the real 15. Those 15 permuted gains are folds within a single draw and share a mask, so the effective null sample size is one and the test treats it as fifteen. The headline is a difference between a measured quantity and a single draw of a random one, reported with no interval. This runs B=50 INDEPENDENT permutations per dataset, giving the null distribution, a permutation p-value with the +1 correction, and a percentile interval. It also extends the bound from the 8 datasets that carried it to all 12 the suite wires, which is the concession section 7 makes explicitly. PREDICTION: the sign survives -- mean excess stays negative and the real ceiling stays below the permuted mean on a majority of datasets -- but the per-dataset magnitudes move, because a single draw of a random quantity is not its mean. A 12-permutation probe on hepatitis already moved excess from -0.0089 to -0.0072, same sign, 19% smaller. WHAT WOULD MATTER: if the mean excess crosses zero, or if the real ceiling is above the permuted mean on most datasets, Paper 3's headline is wrong and the paper becomes a different one. That is the risk being taken deliberately -- the current design cannot tell a stable property from an unlucky mask, and shipping it unfixed would be indefensible in review.
